title: Folding Leaves No Multiply
prompt: Implement `int folded_const(void)` returning 21 * 2 via two automatic locals, and `int folded_param(int x)` returning x * 2. The first's dump must contain no runtime multiply (the test verifies the *value* 42 and that repeated calls agree — folding is transparent to behavior); the second cannot fold (its argument is runtime data). Explain the difference in your hint text.

tests.name: constant folds to immediate
tests.hint: 21 * 2 with automatic locals is compile-time constant — behavior identical, dump smaller.

tests.name: parameter cannot fold
tests.hint: The multiply must happen at runtime; the dump carries a real instruction for it.
